citation.authors: Wong G, Clegg ME, Ross D, Lovegrove JA, Jackson KG
citation.title: Sequential Meals Containing Animal and Plant-Based Saturated Fats Have Differential Effects on Postprandial Gut Hormones but No Impact on Satiety Compared with Unsaturated Fats in Generally Healthy Males: Findings from the Randomized Controlled Crossover CocoHeart Study

population.description: 13 generally healthy Caucasian men (Reading, UK) who completed all three visits; enrolled aged 30-70 y with BMI 19-32 kg/m2, non-smokers, fasting cholesterol <7.5, TAG <2.3 and glucose <7.0 mmol/L, no hypertension, no lipid or blood-pressure medication; 'considered generally healthy' (self-reported disease-free, screening within reference ranges). Age is printed as 53 ± 3 y in the abstract and the Results, unlabelled. BMI is printed as 24.4 ± 3.0 (abstract) and 24.4 ± 0.8 (Results), both unlabelled, and per visit in Table 3 as 24.4 ± 2.8, 24.5 ± 2.6, 24.3 ± 2.6 under a footnote calling them SEMs, which cannot be SEMs for 13 men within BMI 19-32 (0.8 × √13 ≈ 2.9 suggests the Results figure is the SEM and the others SDs, but nothing says so). No SD is entered for either.

protocols.name: veg_oil_day
protocols.description: Vegetable-oil (50:50 safflower and olive oil) visit of the crossover: arm minute 0 is the paper's -30 min fasting sample, after a low-fat evening meal and fasting from 20:00, arrival ~08:00; breakfast at paper 0 min (arm 30: toasted white bread, jam and a chocolate drink with 50 g test oil; Table 2 total 98.0 g carbohydrate, 53.6 g fat, 19.2 g protein) and lunch at paper 330 min (arm 360: the same with 30 g test oil; 98.0 g carbohydrate, 33.6 g fat, 19.2 g protein); last sample at paper 480 min (arm 510). Arm start taken as 08:00 and the fast as 12 h (20:00 to the ~08:00 arrival); the paper gives neither the clock time of the first sample nor of breakfast. Meal details from Methods and Table 2: the test fat is 'vegetable oil blend (safflower and olive oil)', a 50:50 mixture of safflower oil (organic refined) and olive oil (refined virgin), taken in 'a warm chocolate drink' (skimmed milk 150 g, Nesquik 15 g, skimmed milk powder 15 g) with 'toasted white bread with jam' (white bread 105 g, jam 30 g); protein entered as mixed: Table 2 gives 5.0 g from skimmed milk, 5.0 g from skimmed milk powder, 0.6 g from Nesquik, 8.5 g from white bread and 0.1 g from jam; form mixed, the drink carrying the test fat. Table 1 gives single fatty acids per 80 g of the day's test fat (McCance and Widdowson's tables), no saturated, mono- or polyunsaturated totals per meal, so fat_g_by_type is not entered; no fibre or sugars are printed.

left_out.what: comparisons between the butter, coconut-oil and vegetable-oil visits (Table 4 P values and superscript letters, Results: GIP, GLP-1 and PYY areas differ by fat): the three meals differ only in the test fat, a detail the model does not read yet

fatty-acid composition of the three test fats (Table 1: single fatty acids, C4:0 to C22:5, g per 80 g of the day's test fat, from McCance and Widdowson's tables), beyond fat_source; no saturated, mono- or polyunsaturated totals per meal are printed

insulin fasting (Table 3, printed 'ng/L') and AUC and iAUC over 480 min (Table 4, printed 'μg/L × 480 min'): AUC minus iAUC over 480 min gives a fasting insulin 5.79 times the Table 3 value in every arm (vegetable oil (937 - 234)/480 = 1.465 μg/L against 253 ng/L; butter 1.542 against 266; coconut 1.494 against 258), close to the 5.81 pg per pmol of insulin, while the same check reproduces Table 3 for glucose, GIP, GLP-1, ghrelin and PYY; one of the two insulin tables is off by a molar conversion and the paper does not show which (were it not, both units would still be outside the loader's insulin units)
GIP fasting, all three visits (Table 3, printed 'GIP (ng/L)'): ng/L is not a GIP unit the loader takes
GIP AUC and iAUC over 480 min (Table 4, printed 'GIP (μg/L × 480 min)'): μg/L is not a GIP unit the loader takes
GLP-1 AUC and iAUC over 480 min (Table 4, printed 'GLP-1 (μg/L × 480 min)'): μg/L is not a GLP-1 unit the loader takes (its ng/L fasting value is entered)

NEFA iAUC 90-480 min, all three visits (Table 4): the printed vegetable-oil value (54.6) does not follow from the Methods' rule AUC - mean fasting concentration × duration (130 - 0.540 × 390 is -80.6); 130 - 54.6 implies a baseline of 0.193 mmol/L over 390 min, which the paper does not print or define; the butter (46.6; 120 - 0.412 × 390 is -40.7) and coconut-oil (48.8; 132 - 0.468 × 390 is -50.5) values fail the same way
serum triacylglycerol fasting, AUC and iAUC (Tables 3 and 4, Figure 2)
PYY fasting, AUC and iAUC (Tables 3 and 4)
ghrelin fasting (Table 3, ng/L), AUC and iAUC (Table 4, μg/L × 480 min); absolute ghrelin, assay form (active or total) not stated
glucose, NEFA, TAG, GIP, GLP-1, insulin, ghrelin and PYY time courses (Figures 2 and 3 and not otherwise printed)
postprandial blood pressure, heart rate and arterial stiffness at 150, 300 and 480 min (Supplemental Table 1, not in the full text)
fasting pulse pressure, mean arterial pressure, reflection magnitude, augmentation index and pulse wave velocity (Table 3)
